mainEntity.name: How does a garage conversion compare to building a new room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Converting an existing attached garage into living space is often faster and uses existing foundation and wall framing, whereas building a new addition creates custom space from the ground up without sacrificing vehicle storage. The practical tradeoff comes down to vehicle shelter versus yard impact. A garage conversion eliminates covered parking and often requires leveling concrete slabs, insulating exterior walls, and upgrading HVAC capacity. Building a new addition leaves parking intact and allows you to customize ceiling heights and room layouts, but it requires fresh excavation and foundation pours.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion repurposes existing structure and can be faster, but you lose parking. A new addition preserves garage space and allows custom sizing, but requires new ground-up construction.
